chunks: And from him, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from 'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man has female slaves (concubines) and is unable to have intercourse with them; he does something to please them with it. He said: 'As for what is from his body, there is no harm with it.'

key_terms.مِنْ جَسَدِهِ: From his body (referring to physical contact/actions)
key_terms.يُلَذِّذُهُنَّ: To please them / to delight them

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man deriving pleasure from his concubines if he cannot have intercourse with them?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the permissibility of deriving pleasure from concubines when consummation is not possible, specifically permitting acts involving the body itself. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic view on the sexual rights of concubines, distinguishing between bodily contact and other forms of gratification. It highlights the flexibility in marital laws regarding non-consummated unions within the framework of *Uqr* (concubinage).
